title: The Sealed Western-Style Window
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Ran, Sonoko, Eisuke, Kogoro -- who solves the case remotely by phone/note and lets Officer Yamamura take public credit) omitted by convention, per the ep011 prototype. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. The old lower-fidelity case file (cases/ep446-447...) had the correct culprit (Kuramoto), correct victim, and correct core motive/method summary, so no culprit correction was needed here -- but it was extremely thin: it omitted the villa's full backstory (the older brother built the secret passage specifically to spy on his wife's affair with his younger brother, then killed her and staged his own suicide, a case Kuramoto's crime consciously or unconsciously replicates), the actual physical clue chain (the encyclopedia volumes left out of order -- 6,3,4,1 -- when Kuramoto crept back to fix them after overhearing Conan mention the order, and the anomalous window-spacing/room-size comparison across the villa's four bedrooms that gave away the hidden passage), the discarded elastic-key-holder locked-room theory floated and dropped mid-episode, the chair-position red herring Officer Yamamura initially misread as proof of murder, and Officer Yamamura's own active role (investigating, secretly hiding in Kuramoto's room, and making the arrest). All of that is restored here. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Unlike the villa's other three bedrooms, the maid's room alone has narrow window spacing and a window set oddly close to the wall -- the anomaly that gives away the hidden passage.
